opportunity.buyer: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation, Division of Fish & Wildlife
opportunity.project_name: Hale Creek Field Station Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS)
opportunity.response_format: Microsoft Office product or Adobe PDF
opportunity.response_subject: Hale Creek Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS)

questions.text: Sample login: replace the current Microsoft Access workflow; support multiple aliquots, barcode labels, collection chain of custody, and internal laboratory chain of custody.
Sample preparation: replace the current Microsoft Access PCB / organochlorine-pesticide preparation workflow and support additional preparation workflows.
Sample processing: replace the current Microsoft Access processing-parameter workflow and support observations and pictures.
Import results from all laboratory instruments and support manual sample and test-result entry.
Track consumables and solvent inventory.
Manage agency standard operating procedures and quality-control information.

Provide analytical-run reports, QC and process-control charts, ad-hoc reports, work lists, preparation lists, run lists, sample-result reports, sample-status reports, and consumable/reagent traceability.
Import legacy databases and preserve access to archived data according to agency policies.
Provide staff training.
Follow applicable New York State and DEC policies, laws, and compliance requirements.
Follow New York State Office of Information Technology Services policies and standards.
Be highly available, modular, and scalable.
Allow users to define future workflows, analytical methods, and equipment.
Identify whether proposed products are available on a New York State contract or Federal GSA contract and provide the contract number if applicable.
Describe the ability to offer a LIMS that meets the Desired Requirements.
Describe hybrid on-site / cloud storage, if applicable.
Describe remote management of software, if applicable.
Describe the maintenance and support program and any additional costs.
Describe disaster-recovery capabilities.
Describe network, server, and equipment requirements.
Describe warranties, installation, training, and ongoing maintenance.
Describe equipment-replacement provisions.
Identify existing customers with implementations of similar scope and size.
Provide a feasible implementation plan requiring minimal DEC / NYS ITS support.
Describe hybrid on-site / cloud deployment, if applicable.
Provide company personnel count, years in business, and special government or sensitive clearances / ratings, if any.
Identify partners and responsibilities; if partners are not selected, describe desired partner types and responsibilities.
Provide New York State OGS or Federal GSA contract information, if applicable.
